messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Patterns & Pivots: QBR prep — week of Apr 7

Team —

Quick rollup for leadership distribution ahead of Friday's QBR dry run. Kept this tight so execs can skim; attaching a one-pager (QBR-patterns-pivots-v1.pdf).

Top wins (last 7d):
- Hosted API latencies: p50 down 12% after runtime kernel tweak; cost/tokens improved ~6%.
- Closed two Dedicated pilot commitments (one inbound from Nimbus Health, details below).
- Console: token-level trace rollout completed for 40% of routes — caught a batching regression we fixed.

Key risks / signals:
1) Nimbus Health (potential enterprise) flagged a 95th percentile latency spike on long-chat sessions; they asked for a predictable Dedicated throughput SLA. Sales + Eng need to align on a contract-level latency target vs. burst availability.
2) QBR narrative: we need a clearer cost/unit story for Dedicated vs. Hosted for the slides — ops requested a small table comparing real customer workloads.
3) Legal asked for proposed amendment language for dedicated capacity trials (see related link HS-Deal-12547).

Asks (what I need from you by EOD Thursday):
- Laura: can you surface a short metric row (p50/p95/p999) for the affected routes + sample logs? Needs to fit one slide.
- Jonas: ops runbook update — draft a mitigation bullet (owner & ETA) for the Nimbus performance mode and include any configuration changes we plan.
- Karthik & Vanessa: confirm whether we want to offer a time-bound SLA credit (yes/no) for pilot commits, and if yes, the refundable band.

I'm looping in Alice (Nimbus) on the thread below; I want to be transparent about what we plan to present at the QBR and ensure we're not promising beyond the trial.

Attachments: QBR-patterns-pivots-v1.pdf

Thanks —
Sean
Sean Gallagher
VP, Platform Operations

Sean / Laura —

I've drafted the ops mitigation entry and attached a short action tracker (Nimbus-action-items-20270407.xlsx). High level:
- Root cause (interim): KV-cache thrash on long chat sessions when sequence length >2k under mixed batching. We see elevated tail latency when a small portion of requests have very long context.
- Immediate mitigation (owner: Ops-Runbook): enforce a soft-shed for >3k token sessions during bursts + auto-fallback to a lower-quantized model variant for long sessions. ETA: config change staged Thu 10:00 PDT, full rollout Fri 02:00 PDT.
- Longer-term: evaluate prefix-KV warmup improvements and a per-customer QoS routing policy to pin Nimbus to Dedicated when trial SLA is accepted (owner: Network & Routing).

I also forwarded the customer's ask below for context. I'm not suggesting we promise an SLA in the QBR — only that we propose a pilot with measurable latency targets and a follow-up technical plan.
